questionText:
Node X has a TCP connection open to node Y. The packets from X to Y go through an intermediate IP router R. Ethernet switch S is the first switch on the network path between X and R. Consider a packet sent from X to Y over this connection.

Which of the following statements is/are TRUE about the destination IP and MAC addresses on this packet at the time it leaves X?
options: The destination IP address is the IP address of R
The destination IP address is the IP address of Y
The destination MAC address is the MAC address of S
The destination MAC address is the MAC address of Y
explanation:
Step 1: Understanding Destination IP Address
The IP address represents the ultimate end-to-end destination of the packet. Throughout its journey across routers, the destination IP address remains the IP address of the destination host, which is node $Y$.

Step 2: Understanding Destination MAC Address
MAC addresses are used for hop-by-hop delivery at the Data Link Layer (Layer 2). To send a packet outside its local subnet to node $Y$, node $X$ must send the frame to its default gateway, which is router $R$. Therefore, the destination MAC address is set to the MAC address of router $R$.

Step 3: Role of Ethernet Switch S
Ethernet switch $S$ is a Layer 2 transparent device that forwards frames within the local network based on MAC addresses. It does not act as a Layer 3 or Layer 2 destination for node $X$.

Summary at the time packet leaves X:
• Destination IP address = IP address of $Y$
• Destination MAC address = MAC address of $R$

Hence, only statement (B) is TRUE.
